evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is three short first-person paragraphs (116 words) that ask for a product and say why. instruction.md:1 'I'd like a small local playground for working on JavaScript and complete HTML files. The editor itself matters: I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source. I want to keep the versions that work without losing a draft when another tab saves first.' instruction.md:3 points to the notes ('Please read the six notes in /instructions before building...') and instruction.md:5 states only the delivery contract ('Put the app in /app and serve the workspace at /. I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in.'). None of the defect patterns named in references/quality-checks.md check 1 are present: no numbered acceptance list, no bullets, no table or feature matrix, no 'shall'/'must' (grep for both in instruction.md returns nothing), no framework, file layout or endpoint list. The only build-ish content is the /app location and serving at /, which is the runtime contract required by row 4, not a build recipe. Cross-checks: the 'six notes' count matches the six files in environment/instructions (behaviour, integration, overview, policy, security, ui), which the Dockerfile copies to /instructions (lines 14-15); /assets/seed_data.json exists and has an empty snippets list, consistent with 'there is no starter app to finish'. The frozen template instruction.md is a CHANGE_ME placeholder, so there is no template text to preserve here. Notes (not defects for this row): (a) 'describes the starting scope; there is no starter app to finish' and 'the custom editor, preview, saved snippets and runtime' in instruction.md:3 read slightly more like an author than a requester, but remain plain prose in a consistent first-person voice. (b) The detailed requirements live in the six notes (about 1,900 words); these are prose paragraphs with zero bullet or numbered-list lines and 21 uses of 'must' across all six, i.e. dense but written as notes rather than a spec table. They include a hard implementation constraint (ui.md: 'Don't use a textarea, input or contenteditable element as the document surface, and don't use CodeMirror, Monaco, Ace...'), which is a product-defining constraint stated in prose rather than a build recipe; whether the notes' density is fair belongs to other rows. This row is a reading check on source text; no runtime evidence is required and none was used. The hosted run in the evidence index is on an earlier candidate and is not evidence for this row.
